trails.name: Mt. Gozu
trails.why: Gozu-san, in the middle of the Gozu range, named for its five peaks and said to have been opened by Kobo Daishi in 809.

trails.name: Mt. Washibetsu
trails.why: Washibetsu-dake, 911.1 m, between Noboribetsu and Muroran in Hokkaido, one of the Hokkaido 100 Famous Mountains.

trails.name: Summit near Nagahama (武奈ヶ嶽)
trails.why: Also called Kohoku Bunagatake to tell it apart from Bunagatake in the Hira mountains.

trails.name: Summit near Morioka (箱ヶ森)
trails.why: Hakogamori, 865.5 m, west of Morioka, Iwate.

trails.name: Mt. Kamuinupuri near Teshikaga
trails.why: Mount Kamui, also Kamuinupuri or Mount Mashū, a potentially active volcano, is a parasitic stratovolcano of the Mashū caldera located in the Akan National Park of Hokkaido, Japan.

trails.name: Mount Sanjūsangen
trails.why: Sanjusangen-zan, on the Fukui-Shiga border at the source of the Kita river.

trails.name: Mount Usuki
trails.why: Usuki-yama, 842.1 m, in Okutama, one of the three Tokura mountains.

trails.name: HIgashitokonoo San summit
trails.why: The western end of the Tokonoo range in northern Hyogo, with views to Hyonosen, Sobu-dake and Oe-yama.

trails.name: Mukabakiyama summit
trails.why: A mountain of two peaks, the 831 m male peak and the 809 m female peak, with cliffs near the top and the Mukabaki river to the east.

trails.name: Summit near Mutsu (大尽山)
trails.why: Ozukushi-yama, a lava dome of the Osore volcano, formed before the Usori caldera.

trails.name: Mount Toishi
trails.why: An 826.7 m mountain named after the whetstones once quarried here; a wind cave on its slope keeps a constant temperature and was used by foresters to store seeds.

trails.name: Akasaka-yama summit
trails.why: An 823.6 m peak in the Nosaka mountains on the Takashima Trail, popular for its views and well known among Kansai hikers.

trails.name: Summit near Hakone (鍋嵐)
trails.why: A twin-peaked mountain about 5 km north of Oyama in the southeastern Tanzawa, its forested summit offering almost no view.

trails.name: Mount Apoi
trails.why: Apoi-dake, 810.5 m, in Samani, Hokkaido, at the southwestern end of the Hidaka range.

trails.name: Summit near Hirosaki (甚吉森)
trails.why: Jinkichimori, on the Akita-Aomori border at the source of the Hira river, the largest tributary of the Iwaki.

trails.name: Mount Nishibetsu
trails.why: From the Nishibetsu hut at the eastern foot, the trail passes "Warbler Valley" larch woods and the steep "Patience Slope", then the "Paradise Flat" about 0.5 km below the summit.

trails.name: Summit near Ōdate (諸助山)
trails.why: Its rock is quartz diorite porphyry; the stones of the Oyu Stone Circles were taken by Jomon people from boulders that rolled down from its north slope into the river.

trails.name: Mt. Saihogadake
trails.why: Saihogatake, in Tsuruga, Fukui, one of the three Tsuruga mountains.

trails.name: Summit near Ōdate (大柴峠)
trails.why: The Raiman Kaido, an old road on which copper from the Osarizawa mine was carried by ox to the port of Noheji and on to Nagasaki; the old track survives under bamboo grass.

trails.name: Eno Dake summit
trails.why: About 8 km north of central Nobeoka, a rugged mountain of eroded granite porphyry between Okue-yama and Mukabaki-yama.

trails.name: Mt. Monbetsu
trails.why: Monbetsu-dake, 715 m, in Date, Hokkaido.

trails.name: Summit near Nayoro (九度山)
trails.why: A solitary peak in Nayoro, Hokkaido, once a sacred "Chinomishiri" of the Ainu, now the Piyashiri ski area.

trails.name: Mt. Hanao
trails.why: Hanao-yama, 669 m, in Yamaguchi, with views of the Akiyoshidai plateau and the Sea of Japan.

trails.name: Mt. Eyama
trails.why: Mount E is an active stratovolcano of the Kameda peninsula, which is itself part of the larger Oshima Peninsula.

trails.name: Summit near Ōdate (羽保屋山)
trails.why: A sacred mountain amid low hills, with the shrine of Haboya Okami on its summit; it was a model for recovery from the Kosaka mine's smoke damage.

trails.name: Summit near Hiroshima (阿武山)
trails.why: Abu-san, a mountain in Hiroshima wrapped on three sides by the Ota river.

trails.name: Mt. Omoto
trails.why: Mount Omoto is a mountain located on Ishigaki Island in Okinawa, Japan. Together, with Kabira Bay, it is a nationally designated Place of Scenic Beauty.

trails.name: Mount Eirei
trails.why: Eirei-zan, 521.3 m, in Rausu, Hokkaido.

trails.name: Summit near Rankoshimachi (母衣月山)
trails.why: Horozuki-yama, 503 m, the highest point of the Tsukikoshi range in Hokkaido.

trails.name: Mt. Rebun
trails.why: Mount Rebun is the highest point on Rebun Island in Rebun, Hokkaidō, Japan. The mountain consists of marine sedimentary rocks from the Early Cretaceous period, 149–97 million years ago.

trails.name: Mt. Chibusa
trails.why: Chibusa-yama, 462.6 m, the highest point of the inhabited Ogasawara islands, on Hahajima, with views to Chichijima.

trails.name: Mt. Iyudake
trails.why: A 446 m peak in the Kunigami mountains of northern Okinawa Island, the highest point of Higashi village.

trails.name: Mariyudu Falls
trails.why: Mariudo Falls on the Urauchi river of Iriomote island, Okinawa, one of Japan's 100 best waterfalls.

trails.name: Sanjo Falls
trails.why: Sanjō Falls is a waterfall in Hinoemata, Fukushima Prefecture, Japan, on the Tadami River in Oze National Park.

trails.name: Mt. Akatani
trails.why: A peak on the north ridge of Tsurugi-dake about 4 km away, with a grassy summit covered in alpine flowers, red in autumn, and views of the Kekachi peaks.

trails.name: Mt. Sazaegadake
trails.why: Sazaegatake, in the north of the Tsuruga peninsula, forming with Saihogatake the ridge between Tsuruga and Mihama.

trails.name: Shogen Pass
trails.why: Shogen Pass, on the main Okuchichibu ridge between Saitama and Yamanashi.

trails.name: Amagi Pass
trails.why: Not an old pass but one created by the Amagi Tunnel, completed in 1904 at about 710 m beneath an 830 m ridge.

trails.name: Yomogi Pass
trails.why: Long known as a crossing of the Joetsu border, a commoners' path avoiding official checkpoints, used by peddlers bartering goods between Niigata and Gunma.

trails.name: Pass near Minamiuonuma (清水峠)
trails.why: Shimizu Pass, 1,448 m, between Minakami in Gunma and Minamiuonuma in Niigata.

trails.name: Karisaka Pass
trails.why: Karisaka Pass, 2,082 m, on the main Okuchichibu ridge between Saitama and Yamanashi, counted among Japan's three great passes.

trails.name: Mt. Akita-Komagatake
trails.why: Akita-Komagatake is an active stratovolcano located 10 km east of Tazawa Lake, near the border between Akita and Iwate prefectures on Honshu Island.

trails.name: Neonotaki waterfall
trails.why: Neo Falls on the Nigorigo river; the Osaka area of Gero has more than 200 waterfalls over 5 m high, fed by rivers from Mount Ontake.

trails.name: Mt. Oku-Sangai
trails.why: Okusankai-dake, 1,811 m, in the Atera mountains on the Gifu-Nagano border, one of Japan's 300 Famous Mountains.

trails.name: Minami-Shouji Falls
trails.why: A waterfall at about 1,500 m on the Dondoko stream, named for the mountain ascetics who trained here; one of the three Dondoko falls with the Shiraito and Goshiki falls above.

trails.name: Osutaka-yama summit
trails.why: Osutaka-yama, 1,775 m, one of the three peaks of Mitsutoge-yama near Lake Kawaguchi.

trails.name: Mt. Banzaburo
trails.why: Amagi-san, the mountain range across central Izu peninsula, one of Japan's 100 Famous Mountains.

trails.name: Ohtori Lake
trails.why: A lake at the north foot of Ito-dake in the Asahi mountains, Yamagata, formed when a landslide dammed the river.

trails.name: Lake near Uozu (餓鬼ノ田圃)
trails.why: Gaki-no-tanbo, a wetland in the Kurobe river basin; "gaki no ta" is a local name for mountain ponds.

trails.name: Yashagaike lake
trails.why: Yasha-ga-ike, a pond near the Fukui-Gifu border, the subject of a dragon god legend.
